- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for volatility spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 periods.
- Model exhibits persistent mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive forecasts are rising, true price often reverses; introduce “reversion trigger” if forecast > +15% above recent 7-day average.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: average forecast with true price if sentiment >0.5, or dampen if sentiment <0.5.
